summary: Week 6 performance sync for Acadia pilot. Redwood shows consistent p95 and throughput gains vs incumbent in current lab runs; some variance at high concurrency without KV cache enabled. Agreement to run a 24h head-to-head with KV cache and full traffic shape, Redwood to share security docs and sizing/pricing for dedicated slot. SE tuning items identified: routing thresholds, batching cap, and quantization sanity check.
topics: p95 latency and throughput delta vs baseline
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Okay, morning everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Patel (Customer): Hi this is Priya, Tom's on as well, Rashid and Elena too.
[00:15] Maya: Great. Luis and I from Redwood, plus Priyanka jumped on for the tuning bits. we'll keep to 40 minutes.
[00:24] Tom Hsu: sounds good.
[00:27] Luis (SE): Alright i'm gonna share the bench highlights—i'll try to be quick. note: these are lab numbers, not production traffic yet, but they're representative.
[00:38] [00:38] Luis: So baseline (IncumbentVendorX) p95 for our test prompt set at 20 token average was ~320ms, throughput plateau around 800 rps per minute (we mean rps as req/min here sorry), Redwood p95 was 210ms and sustained throughput 1,200 req/min on same HW profile with current quant and batching.
[01:05] Priya: wait 1,200 req/min? that's quite a jump. what's the concurrency used?
[01:12] Luis: we ran stepped RPS up to 120 RPS, concurrency 8-12 depending on response length. note: with KV caching enabled prefix hits dropped p95 to ~180ms. without KV cache we saw some spike behavior above 90 RPS.
[01:28] Rashid: can you explain the KV cache hit ratio? we haven't used that in incumbent.
[01:33] Luis: sure, in our run with typical dialog traces the prefix hit ratio was ~42% after warmup. that cuts repeated token compute significantly. sometimes the transcript might show K-V cash in auto-transcribe cause of noise.
[01:49] Elena: and the quantization settings? we saw mention of 4-bit in your doc? any quality regression?
[01:55] Priyanka Rao: i can chime in, we did a quick eval on 500 prompts — negligible delta on rouge/f1 for the set they care about; some edge-case hallucination noise but within threshold.
[02:09] Tom: about the hardware parity — are you running identical GPUs as the incumbent?
[02:14] Luis: yes we matched GPU family and memory footprint for the lab (Nvidia T4/ A10 class equivalent). The delta is mostly runtime-level: batching, kernel selection, and the routing fallback which avoids costly cold KV lookups.
[02:29] Priya: what's the p99 look like? our SLOs are tight.
[02:33] Luis: p99 is closer — incumbent ~640ms, Redwood ~470ms in these runs; p99 has more variance. We recommend canarying p99 thresholds in real traffic.
[02:45] Maya: quick note — when we say throughput we are using req/min for the standard bench. I know some teams use qps, apologies for mixed terms earlier.
[02:55] [02:55] Priya: ok. how confident are you that this holds under our mixed traffic (api + streaming)?
[03:03] Luis: mixed traffic is different — streaming responses increase open connection time and reduce effective throughput. our stitched tests included a 30% streaming fraction and we saw throughput drop ~12% but latency p95 stayed similar with proper batching.
[03:18] Rashid: routing and fallback — walk us through failure modes. if capacity is constrained does traffic go to a cheaper variant?
[03:25] Luis: yes by policy we can fallback to a quantized variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost. we can also route to a regional replica. the playbook we shared includes thresholds: if queue depth > X or p95 > Y we trigger fallback and also auto-scale.
[03:39] Tom: SSO / network — do you support SAML and VPC peering? our security team requires KMS and audit logging.
[03:46] Maya: yes, we have SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS/HSM options for private, and audit logs in Redwood Console. we'll send the SOC2 report and VPC peering checklist after the call.
[03:58] Priya: good. also need retention windows for logs — 90 days minimum.
[04:03] Maya: noted, we'll include retention details.
[04:06] Luis: for tuning, three concrete levers we changed this sprint: 1) reduce max batch size for short prompts to avoid head-of-line blocking, 2) prefix/KV cache warmup window to 120s, 3) routing thresholds for immediate fallback at p95>350ms.
[04:21] Priya: Did you try quantize-llm 4-bit vs 8-bit? we need inference quality comparisons.
[04:27] Priyanka: yes — 4-bit preserved quality for our eval set; 8-bit was unchanged but cost savings differ. we recommend running their specific eval set to confirm.
[04:36] Rashid: any unexpected errors in the lab? timeouts?
[04:39] Luis: Mostly transient queue drains during warmup without KV cache; one run had elevated GPU mem fragmentation causing retries — fixed by small kernel selection change.
[04:48] Elena: can you show the cost delta? our CFO will ask.
[04:51] Maya: quick ballpark — at current pilot scale, unit token cost running on Redwood with these optimizations is roughly 18-22% lower than incumbent; we'll send a detailed delta in the pricing sheet.
[05:03] Tom: good. For head-to-head 24h test, what artifacts do you need?
[05:06] Maya: baseline logs, traffic shape (RPS over time), target prompts, and acceptance criteria. we'll also need a test account for the dedicated slot once agreed.
[05:16] Priya: we'll export baseline logs, started. Tom will confirm peering.
[05:19] Luis: one more thing — when we disable KV cache the latency gap narrows; so KV caching is a major lever. if Acadia can't rely on prefix caching due to privacy rules we should discuss prefix hashing or encrypted cache options.
[05:34] Priya: we need to confirm whether we can use prefix caching for PII-containing prompts. security will weigh in.
[05:40] Maya: understood. we'll add encrypted KV cache notes in the security doc.
[05:44] Rashid: about dedicated slot — what's minimum commit?
[05:47] Maya: typical minimum for a dedicated pool starts at 4x A10 equiv for pilot, pricing is in the sheet we'll send; we can do a shorter term monthly pilot with a slight premium.
[05:58] [05:58] Priya: ok, sounds reasonable. expected timeline?
[06:02] Maya: customer to run 24h baseline export and Redwood will run the same head-to-head starting 2026-04-27; follow-up on 2026-05-04 to review results and failover demo.
[06:12] Tom: noted.
[06:14] Luis: final technical recap — routing thresholds updated, batching caps adjusted, KV cache warmup set to 120s, quantization validated on eval set. we'll push the routing policy to the test cluster later today.
[06:29] Priya: thanks. can you also include a quickhowto for interpreting the latency/throughput spreadsheet? our PMs will want a one-pager.
[06:36] Maya: yes one-pager to accompany the spreadsheet.
[06:39] Elena: thanks everyone.
[06:41] Maya: great, we'll follow up with docs and the proposed schedule. thanks all.
[06:46] [END]
